findings.issue_text: AdminPermissions listener will throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2: when fine-grained authz is enabled, client deletion fires ClientRemovedEvent, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws, breaking client removal and leaving stale permission data; same risk for RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent with V2 roles()/groups() evaluators

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission ignores type-level (all clients) grants when a per-client resource exists — it evaluates only the per-client resource and falls back to the all-clients resource only when the per-client resource is null, silently denying admins with valid all-clients MANAGE/VIEW permissions

ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission only scans per-client resources via findByType and misses type-level grants, so admins with all-clients VIEW pass canView but get an empty set from getClientsWithPermission, causing deny-despite-grant list inconsistency

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the token-exchange authorization path with a runtime exception instead of degrading to a defined deny or V1 fallback

hasPermission treats 'resource exists but no policy attached' inconsistently: the fallback branch guards with policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() → false, but the per-client branch has no such guard — the guard logic should be unified

Listener gating change in AdminPermissions strands stale permission data: cleanup only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled at event time, so realms that had the feature disabled after creating permission resources will leak orphaned authorization resources/policies on deletions

ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java calls setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException when V2 evaluator is active, failing client/role/group delete operations or leaving orphaned permission state; V2 path must skip cleanup or branch on evaluator version

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException while unconditionally returned by MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), breaking token-exchange flows with 500 errors instead of deny/grant; callers do not guard the V2 path

Event cleanup for role/client/group removal is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, so if the feature is disabled after permission resources were created, stale authorization resources/policies remain and could reactivate if re-enabled

AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient accepts both internal UUID and clientId, allowing ambiguous resource names that could silently bind permissions to the wrong client and grant cross-client access; should be restricted to one ID namespace like resolveUser

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback creates a type-level resource as a side effect of authorization checks (mutating authz store on read path), and evaluation of type-level resources may conflate CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES scope separation for all clients

getClientsWithPermission performs an unbounded findByType scan over all Clients resources with no pagination or filter, invoking a full hasGrantedPermission/evaluatePermission policy evaluation per resource — an N+1 (potentially quadratic) workload on the hot admin client-listing path (clients().findAll())

canView(ClientModel) triggers 3-4 separate full evaluatePermission invocations per single permission check (canView() plus canConfigure→canManage plus hasPermission), each re-loading the resource server, resource, scopes, and policies
hasPermission(ClientModel, ...) calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) on every invocation as a guard, adding a store round-trip per evaluation

hasPermission/hasGrantedPermission constructs a List (Arrays.asList(scope)) allocation for a single-element contains check inside nested loops over permissions×scopes — a negligible micro-allocation nitpick

setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException while the removal listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls it on ClientRemovedEvent, causing client/role/group deletions to fail or leak 500s when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides public ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissions methods (canExchangeTo, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, etc.) with UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the V1 admin REST contract and returning 500s to API consumers instead of a versioned 4xx or migrated behavior

Asymmetric fallback in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String): a per-client resource with no matching grant blocks the all-clients grant, denying users who hold type-level MANAGE/VIEW permissions

resolveClient accepts a client by internal id or clientId but ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission looks up resources exclusively by client.getId(), so resources keyed by clientId are silently missed and evaluation denies
Public interface javadoc on ClientPermissionEvaluator.canManage/canView drifts from actual behavior, describing per-implementation (V1/V2) behavior rather than a stable contract

Test-helper signature churn in AbstractPermissionTest: methods changed from instance methods to static with an added ManagedClient parameter, potentially breaking other subclasses not shown in the truncated diff
Client-removal event handler calls setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2 (ClientPermissionsV2), breaking client deletion and orphaning authz resources

Gating the cleanup listener on Profile.isFeatureEnabled creates stale-orphan risk: if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled after permissions were created, removed roles/clients/groups leave dangling Resource/Policy entries in the authz store
canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing unhandled 500 errors for V1 callers in token-exchange admin flows with no fallback handling
hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback path lacks a null check on getResourceTypeResource result before calling getScopes(), unlike the sibling hasPermission(String) method

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback only considers policies attached directly to the type resource via findByResource, potentially missing scope permissions defined with resourceType=Clients, leading to over-denying or over-allowing evaluation
getClientsWithPermission: hasGrantedPermission re-fetches realmResourceServer() and dereferences server without a null check, risking NPE; should reuse the already-validated server reference
ClientPermissionsV2 cache in MgmtPermissionsV2 is not session-scoped-safe: if a MgmtPermissionsV2 instance is cached across sessions, the retained KeycloakSession/RealmModel causes stale evaluation
Test hygiene: @AfterEach cleanup deletes all scope permissions but createAllPermission/createPermission do not register their own cleanup, risking cross-test permission leakage and flaky failures

New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope has zero test coverage, including the code path that grants it — PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient never creates a map-roles-client-scope permission or exercises a client-scope role-mapping operation, so a regression in hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) would pass CI.

No test that type-level (all-clients) permissions still apply when a per-client resource already exists — ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to the type-level resource only if resource == null, so once a per-client resource exists, type-level MANAGE/VIEW policies are silently ignored for that client; the combined case is untested in both directions.

Behavioral change in AdminPermissions.registerListener (feature gating via Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) has no corresponding test verifying cleanup still runs when the feature is enabled or is safely skipped (no NPE on management()) when disabled.

Many UnsupportedOperationException overrides in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) are untested, and no test proves reachable admin REST flows don't hit them — notably the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so a client deletion would throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2.

getClientsWithPermission semantics (wildcard "Clients" entry vs. concrete client ids) is untested for mixed grants — no test covers the combination of a type-level grant plus per-client grants, or how callers should interpret the wildcard; hasGrantedPermission evaluates against the current session's admin identity inside a store callback.

No tests for canList / canListClientScopes / query-roles paths documented in the new javadoc in ClientPermissionEvaluator — PermissionClientTest never tests a user with only query roles, and the @AfterEach list assertions only test manage/view grants.

Dead/unreachable private getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 — only used by the throwing canExchangeTo; untestable dead code signaling the token-exchange story for V2 clients is unresolved and unverified by tests.

ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions but throws UnsupportedOperationException from 14 inherited methods, breaking LSP and potentially crashing runtime callers such as the ClientRemovedEvent listener calling setPermissionsEnabled, causing client deletion to throw

Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2: hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) all contain identical evaluate/loop/match logic; extract a shared evaluate helper

hasPermission overloads resolve the 'all clients' resource inconsistently: hasPermission(String) uses resourceStore.findByName while hasPermission(ClientModel, String) uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA plus a policy-store existence check, inviting inconsistent behavior
Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2: unused private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) and unused static import AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE
canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) duplicate the role+permission logic of canManage and should delegate to single-scope helpers
Interface javadoc in ClientPermissionEvaluator leaks V1/V2 implementation knowledge ('For V2 only: ...'), which will become stale; version-specific semantics belong in implementing classes' docs

registerListener feature check wraps the entire event-handling block, disabling pre-existing role/group/permission cleanup handlers too; the overly broad guard and its coupling to V2's throwing setPermissionsEnabled needs explicit commentary or narrowing

Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2: AdminPermissions.java listener cleanup calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent, which throws under ClientPermissionsV2, failing client removal or erroring on every delete when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; same hazard applies to RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent if V2 role/group evaluators share the same throwing stub

canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 lost the admin-role fallback, so a realm admin with MANAGE_CLIENTS who passes canManage(client) is denied on mapping client roles, composites, or client-scope roles, breaking normal admin flows

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback in ClientPermissionsV2 misses type-based permissions: when the per-client resource doesn't exist, the all-clients fallback gates on findByResource which doesn't return type-associated scope permissions, causing valid global grants to silently deny; this deny path is untested

canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, yielding a 500 in token-exchange admin checks instead of a clean deny or routed V1 evaluation

Feature-flag gate on cleanup listeners in AdminPermissions.java skips authz resource cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled, leaving stale orphaned resources/policies if the feature is toggled off after permissions were created
getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 performs N+1 full policy-engine evaluations per client resource with no caching, a likely performance cliff on large realms

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions listener will throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2: when fine-grained authz is enabled, client deletion fires ClientRemovedEvent, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws, breaking client removal and leaving stale permission data; same risk for RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent with V2 roles()/groups() evaluators

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In MgmtPermissionsV2, clients() is overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). If the listener runs in the V2 permissions mode (MgmtPermissionsV2), client deletion would trigger this exception and break cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission ignores type-level (all clients) grants when a per-client resource exists — it evaluates only the per-client resource and falls back to the all-clients resource only when the per-client resource is null, silently denying admins with valid all-clients MANAGE/VIEW permissions

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code always prefers the per-client resource when it exists (`resourceStore.findByName(..., client.getId(), ...)`) and only falls back to the type-level “all-clients” resource when the per-client resource is `null`. If a per-client resource exists (e.g., due to some other permission previously created for that client) but the caller only has a valid grant on the type-level resource ("all clients" MANAGE/VIEW/etc.), this method never evaluates that type-level permission and will return `false`. This contradicts the intended behavior described in the new/updated Javadoc (V2 should also honor permissions for MANAGE/VIEW all clients).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission only scans per-client resources via findByType and misses type-level grants, so admins with all-clients VIEW pass canView but get an empty set from getClientsWithPermission, causing deny-despite-grant list inconsistency

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, global/all-clients grants are evaluated via hasPermission(String scope), which explicitly looks up the type-level resource by name (resourceStore.findByName(..., AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)) and can make canView()/canManage() true without any per-client resources existing. But getClientsWithPermission(scope) only iterates resources returned by resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds resource.getName() for those resources; it has no fallback to the type-level “all-clients” resource nor any expansion from an all-clients grant to actual client IDs. This creates an inconsistency where a caller can be globally granted (e.g., VIEW all clients) while getClientsWithPermission may return no client IDs (or not the expected set), leading to deny/filtering issues depending on how the set is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the token-exchange authorization path with a runtime exception instead of degrading to a defined deny or V1 fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and several other permission-building methods) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is now wired to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, any V2 code path that invokes token-exchange-related methods would fail at runtime rather than returning a defined denial. However, the diff does not show any invocation of these methods (or the token-exchange path), so the claim that it definitively "breaks" token-exchange cannot be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission treats 'resource exists but no policy attached' inconsistently: the fallback branch guards with policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() → false, but the per-client branch has no such guard — the guard logic should be unified

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String)`, the fallback path (when per-client `Resource` is null) explicitly short-circuits if `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`, while the normal per-client path evaluates permissions even if that per-client resource has no policies attached. This is a real inconsistency in control flow shown in the diff, but it does not clearly change correctness because `evaluatePermission(...)` would typically yield no granted scopes anyway, resulting in `false` in both cases. The issue is thus more about consistency/efficiency/clarity than a verifiable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Listener gating change in AdminPermissions strands stale permission data: cleanup only runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled at event time, so realms that had the feature disabled after creating permission resources will leak orphaned authorization resources/policies on deletions

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` wraps all deletion-event handling (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`, whereas previously it always called `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on those removals. This is a real behavior change: if the feature is disabled at the time of a deletion, the cleanup/disable logic will not run, which can leave previously-created fine-grained authz artifacts untouched. Whether that is an actual defect depends on expected behavior when toggling the feature, which isn’t shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java calls setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException when V2 evaluator is active, failing client/role/group delete operations or leaving orphaned permission state; V2 path must skip cleanup or branch on evaluator version

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.java, the ProviderEventListener still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` (now gated only by `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`). This diff introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` and wires it via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`, but `ClientPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Therefore, when the V2 permissions implementation is the one returned by `management(...).clients()`, a client removal event will trigger an exception during cleanup, potentially breaking delete flows or preventing proper cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException while unconditionally returned by MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), breaking token-exchange flows with 500 errors instead of deny/grant; callers do not guard the V2 path

adjudication.rationale: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns a ClientPermissionsV2 instance (no feature/usage guard in this method), and ClientPermissionsV2 overrides several ClientPermissions methods to throw UnsupportedOperationException, including canExchangeTo(...) and exchangeToPermission(...). If any existing runtime flow (e.g., token exchange authorization checks) invokes these methods through the clients() permission evaluator when V2 is active, it will result in an unhandled runtime exception (likely 500) rather than a permission decision. The diff shows the unconditional wiring plus the throwing overrides; it does not show any compensating guard at the call sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Event cleanup for role/client/group removal is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag, so if the feature is disabled after permission resources were created, stale authorization resources/policies remain and could reactivate if re-enabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the removal-event listener logic in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`), so `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` will no longer run for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, or `GroupRemovedEvent` when the feature flag is off. From the diff alone, this does imply that if fine-grained authz data already exists and the feature is later disabled, subsequent removals won’t trigger this cleanup path, potentially leaving orphaned authz artifacts. However, the claim that they "could reactivate" when re-enabled is speculative and not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient accepts both internal UUID and clientId, allowing ambiguous resource names that could silently bind permissions to the wrong client and grant cross-client access; should be restricted to one ID namespace like resolveUser

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `resolveClient` mirrors the existing `resolveUser` pattern: it attempts lookup by internal ID first, then by a human-facing identifier (`clientId`/`username`), and returns the internal ID (`client.getId()` / `user.getId()`). The finding claims `resolveUser` is restricted to a single ID namespace, but in this same file `resolveUser` also accepts both user ID and username. While one could speculate about rare collisions where a `clientId` equals another client's UUID, the diff does not demonstrate any concrete ambiguous “resource name” binding or cross-client permission grant beyond this standard fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback creates a type-level resource as a side effect of authorization checks (mutating authz store on read path), and evaluation of type-level resources may conflate CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES scope separation for all clients

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when a per-client `Resource` is missing it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (see new code around the `// check if there is permission for "all-clients"` comment). Given the surrounding API naming in this diff (`getOrCreateResource` exists in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and schema code is oriented around on-demand resource creation), this call is plausibly a “get-or-create” and may therefore create/type-level resources during an authorization check (a read-path side effect), which is a legitimate architecture/behavior concern introduced by the change. However, the second part of the finding (“conflate CONFIGURE/MANAGE/MAP_ROLES scope separation”) is not directly supported by the diff: the check still looks for the specific expected scope in returned `Permission.getScopes()`, so scope separation is preserved at least at this call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission performs an unbounded findByType scan over all Clients resources with no pagination or filter, invoking a full hasGrantedPermission/evaluatePermission policy evaluation per resource — an N+1 (potentially quadratic) workload on the hot admin client-listing path (clients().findAll())

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String) which calls resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and for each resource executes hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope), which in turn calls root.evaluatePermission(...) (policy evaluation). This is an unpaginated full scan over all "Clients"-typed resources with per-resource evaluation, so the performance/N+1 concern is grounded in the added code. However, the claim that this is on the hot clients().findAll() path is not directly verifiable from the diff (no call sites shown), making it a performance/architecture issue rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canView(ClientModel) triggers 3-4 separate full evaluatePermission invocations per single permission check (canView() plus canConfigure→canManage plus hasPermission), each re-loading the resource server, resource, scopes, and policies

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canView(ClientModel)` is implemented as `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) return true; return hasPermission(client, VIEW);`. `canView()` may call `hasPermission(VIEW)` (which invokes `root.evaluatePermission(...)`), and `canConfigure(client)` may call `canManage(client)` which calls `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)`, then potentially `hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE)`. If those all fail, `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` is called at the end. Each `hasPermission*` method reloads `realmResourceServer()`, looks up the `Resource`, and calls `root.evaluatePermission(...)`. So a single `canView(client)` check can indeed trigger up to ~4 separate `evaluatePermission` invocations and repeated store lookups. This is a diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, ...) calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) on every invocation as a guard, adding a store round-trip per evaluation

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when the per-client `Resource` is missing, the code falls back to the "all clients" resource and then calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` as a guard before evaluation. This introduces an extra policy-store lookup each time this method is invoked in that fallback path (i.e., a store round-trip per check when the client resource doesn't exist), which is a concrete performance/architecture concern shown by the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission/hasGrantedPermission constructs a List (Arrays.asList(scope)) allocation for a single-element contains check inside nested loops over permissions×scopes — a negligible micro-allocation nitpick

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Arrays.asList(scope)` used in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String)` and `hasPermission(String)` to do a `contains` check, but this is a minor micro-optimization/style nit (could be `scope.equals(s)`) and not a meaningful review issue or defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException while the removal listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls it on ClientRemovedEvent, causing client/role/group deletions to fail or leak 500s when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the listener handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is newly overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). If the management(...) call resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under this feature (consistent with the added V2 classes), client removal will trigger an UnsupportedOperationException during event handling, potentially failing deletions or surfacing 500s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides public ClientPermissionEvaluator/ClientPermissions methods (canExchangeTo, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, etc.) with UnsupportedOperationException, breaking the V1 admin REST contract and returning 500s to API consumers instead of a versioned 4xx or migrated behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class (returned by `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`) overrides multiple public permission-management methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) and unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any existing admin REST/resource code path invokes these methods while running with the V2 permissions implementation, this will surface as an unhandled runtime exception (typically a 500). The diff does not show guards or alternative handling at call sites, but it does verifiably introduce these UOE stubs, creating a concrete risk/contract concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric fallback in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String): a per-client resource with no matching grant blocks the all-clients grant, denying users who hold type-level MANAGE/VIEW permissions

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`). It only falls back to the type-level "all clients" resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) when that per-client resource is `null`. If a per-client resource exists but does not yield the requested scope in evaluation, the method returns `false` without ever evaluating the type-level resource. This means a user with a type-level grant (e.g., MANAGE/VIEW on all clients) can be denied for a specific client merely because a per-client resource exists without a matching grant, matching the finding’s described asymmetric fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveClient accepts a client by internal id or clientId but ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission looks up resources exclusively by client.getId(), so resources keyed by clientId are silently missed and evaluation denies

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), when resourceType is CLIENTS it calls resolveClient(session, id), and resolveClient returns client.getId() even if the input was a clientId (it first tries getClientById, then getClientByClientId, but always returns the internal id). Therefore resources created via this path will be named by internal client id, matching ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission() which looks up resources by client.getId(). The diff does not show any path creating client resources keyed by clientId that would be missed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public interface javadoc on ClientPermissionEvaluator.canManage/canView drifts from actual behavior, describing per-implementation (V1/V2) behavior rather than a stable contract

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `ClientPermissionEvaluator` gains extensive public Javadoc that explicitly documents implementation-specific behavior (e.g., multiple methods say “For V2 only: Also if it has permission to ...” such as `canManage()`, `canView()`, `canManageClientScopes()`, etc.). This couples the interface contract to particular implementations (`ClientPermissionsV2` vs existing behavior in `ClientPermissions`) rather than defining a stable, implementation-agnostic contract for the evaluator. While not a runtime defect, it is a concrete API/documentation design concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test-helper signature churn in AbstractPermissionTest: methods changed from instance methods to static with an added ManagedClient parameter, potentially breaking other subclasses not shown in the truncated diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AbstractPermissionTest` changing helpers like `getPermissionsResource()`, `getScopePermissionsResource()`, and `createPermission(...)` from instance methods to `static` methods that now require an explicit `ManagedClient client` parameter. Several subclasses in the diff were updated to pass `client`, but the finding’s concern about potentially breaking other subclasses outside the truncated diff is plausible: any existing tests calling the old instance methods would fail to compile until updated. This is a real refactor/API-churn concern, but the actual breakage cannot be verified from the shown diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-removal event handler calls setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2 (ClientPermissionsV2), breaking client deletion and orphaning authz resources

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) is overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under V2/feature-enabled execution, a client removal event would trigger an exception in the listener, plausibly breaking client deletion cleanup and leaving related authz data unmanaged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gating the cleanup listener on Profile.isFeatureEnabled creates stale-orphan risk: if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled after permissions were created, removed roles/clients/groups leave dangling Resource/Policy entries in the authz store

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the provider event listener cleanup logic in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`). Previously, `RoleRemovedEvent`/`ClientRemovedEvent`/`GroupRemovedEvent` always called `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which likely performs authz-store cleanup/disable for removed entities. With the new gate, if fine-grained authz is turned off after permissions were created, subsequent removals will skip this cleanup entirely, leaving any existing authz resources/policies for those removed IDs untouched in the authz store (dangling/orphan entries).

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo / exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2, causing unhandled 500 errors for V1 callers in token-exchange admin flows with no fallback handling

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides several `ClientPermissions` methods (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, etc.) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this V2 implementation, so any code path running under V2 that invokes these methods would fail at runtime (likely surfacing as a 500 if uncaught). However, the finding’s specific claim about "V1 callers" and "token-exchange admin flows" is not verifiable from this diff because no calling endpoints/flows are shown here, and it may be an intentional non-support in V2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback path lacks a null check on getResourceTypeResource result before calling getScopes(), unlike the sibling hasPermission(String) method
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying risk: getResourceTypeResource may return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, and the code then dereferences it without a defensive null check (golden mentions findByResource; candidate mentions getScopes()). The core issue is the missing null handling leading to potential NullPointerException.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback only considers policies attached directly to the type resource via findByResource, potentially missing scope permissions defined with resourceType=Clients, leading to over-denying or over-allowing evaluation

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when the per-client Resource is missing it falls back to the type resource and then short-circuits based on authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty(). This check only detects policies directly linked to that concrete Resource. Scope permissions created using only resourceType=Clients (no resources) may not be returned by a “findByResource” lookup, causing the method to return false without performing evaluation, i.e., incorrectly denying access even though a resourceType-based permission exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission: hasGrantedPermission re-fetches realmResourceServer() and dereferences server without a null check, risking NPE; should reuse the already-validated server reference

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, `server` is fetched once and null-checked, but the helper `hasGrantedPermission(Resource resource, String scope)` re-fetches `root.realmResourceServer()` and then immediately uses it when constructing `new ResourcePermission(..., server)` without a null check. While `hasGrantedPermission` is only called from `getClientsWithPermission` (which already validated a `server`), the re-fetch is unnecessary and weakens the null-safety guarantee; reusing the already-validated `server` would avoid any potential NPE if `realmResourceServer()` were to return null later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 cache in MgmtPermissionsV2 is not session-scoped-safe: if a MgmtPermissionsV2 instance is cached across sessions, the retained KeycloakSession/RealmModel causes stale evaluation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows MgmtPermissionsV2 adds a cached field `private ClientPermissionsV2 clientPermissions;` and returns a lazily-created instance in `clients()` using the current `session`, `realm`, and `authz`. However, nothing in the diff shows that a `MgmtPermissionsV2` instance itself is cached or reused across Keycloak sessions; the finding’s core claim (“cached across sessions… causes stale evaluation”) depends on lifecycle/caching behavior not evidenced in this PR diff. Within a single MgmtPermissionsV2 instance, caching is consistent with the existing `userPermissions` pattern already present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test hygiene: @AfterEach cleanup deletes all scope permissions but createAllPermission/createPermission do not register their own cleanup, risking cross-test permission leakage and flaky failures

adjudication.rationale: In `AbstractPermissionTest`, the new helper methods `createAllPermission(...)` and `createPermission(...)` ultimately call `ScopePermissionsResource.create(...)` but do not register any cleanup (unlike `createUserPolicy` / `createClientPolicy`, which add `realm.cleanup()` removals). Some test classes in the diff add `@AfterEach` cleanup that deletes all scope permissions (e.g., `PermissionClientTest`, `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, `UserResourceTypePermissionTest`), but that hygiene is not enforced by the helpers themselves and is not shown for all tests using these helpers (e.g., `PermissionRESTTest` has no cleanup in the diff). This is a test-isolation concern that could lead to cross-test state leakage if cleanup is missed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope has zero test coverage, including the code path that grants it — PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient never creates a map-roles-client-scope permission or exercises a client-scope role-mapping operation, so a regression in hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) would pass CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces the new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` (AdminPermissionsSchema) and new authorization logic that checks it (`ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles()` -> `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). In the added/modified tests, `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants only `MAP_ROLES`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`, and `CONFIGURE` for the client (`createPermission(... Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) ...)`) and does not grant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` nor exercise an operation that would require it. No other test in the shown diff appears to create a permission with `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` or validate `hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`, so a regression specific to that scope could go undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that type-level (all-clients) permissions still apply when a per-client resource already exists — ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to the type-level resource only if resource == null, so once a per-client resource exists, type-level MANAGE/VIEW policies are silently ignored for that client; the combined case is untested in both directions.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource by `client.getId()`. It only falls back to the type-level ("all-clients") resource when `resource == null`. If a per-client resource exists (e.g., created due to some other per-client permission), the method evaluates permissions solely against that per-client resource and never considers any type-level policies for `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. This means global MANAGE/VIEW/etc. policies can be ignored for clients that already have a resource, leading to incorrect authorization outcomes. The added tests cover type-level-only and per-client-only scenarios but do not cover the mixed case where both exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in AdminPermissions.registerListener (feature gating via Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) has no corresponding test verifying cleanup still runs when the feature is enabled or is safely skipped (no NPE on management()) when disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `AdminPermissions.registerListener` to wrap all event-handling cleanup (`roles().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. This is a nontrivial behavioral change: when the feature is disabled, the listener now skips cleanup entirely. The diff adds/updates multiple FGAP-related tests, but none exercise this listener behavior for either enabled or disabled feature states. That makes the review point about missing coverage for this gating specific and grounded in the diff, but it’s not a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Many UnsupportedOperationException overrides in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) are untested, and no test proves reachable admin REST flows don't hit them — notably the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so a client deletion would throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes it possible for a client deletion event to call an implementation that throws. In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. In V2, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (along with several other overrides). If the V2 management implementation is used under this feature flag, a client removal will trigger this call path and throw at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission semantics (wildcard "Clients" entry vs. concrete client ids) is untested for mixed grants — no test covers the combination of a type-level grant plus per-client grants, or how callers should interpret the wildcard; hasGrantedPermission evaluates against the current session's admin identity inside a store callback.
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that getClientsWithPermission returns the name of the type-level "Clients" resource (a wildcard-like entry) rather than concrete client IDs, while callers expect actual client IDs and may fail (e.g., null client). The candidate explicitly flags the semantic mismatch between a wildcard "Clients" entry and concrete client IDs and notes unclear caller interpretation (though framed as missing tests rather than the specific null-failure path). This is the same underlying concern: wildcard/type-level grant being treated as client identifiers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for canList / canListClientScopes / query-roles paths documented in the new javadoc in ClientPermissionEvaluator — PermissionClientTest never tests a user with only query roles, and the @AfterEach list assertions only test manage/view grants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/expands Javadoc in `ClientPermissionEvaluator` explicitly documenting `canList()` and `canListClientScopes()` behavior involving query roles (e.g., `AdminRoles.QUERY_CLIENTS` / `AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS`), but the newly added/modified tests in `PermissionClientTest` only exercise manage/view/configure/map-roles style grants (e.g., `testManageOnlyOneClient`, `testConfigureOnlyOneClient`, `testManageAllClients`, `testViewAllClients`, `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`) and do not cover scenarios where a caller has only query roles and should be allowed to list (or list client scopes) per the documented contract. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/unreachable private getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 — only used by the throwing canExchangeTo; untestable dead code signaling the token-exchange story for V2 clients is unresolved and unverified by tests.

ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions but throws UnsupportedOperationException from 14 inherited methods, breaking LSP and potentially crashing runtime callers such as the ClientRemovedEvent listener calling setPermissionsEnabled, causing client deletion to throw

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, several inherited API methods are overridden to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` (and also `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, etc.). In the same diff, the admin permissions event listener (`AdminPermissions.registerListener`) handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. Also in this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`. Therefore, in the V2 codepath, a client removal event can trigger `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` and throw at runtime, potentially breaking client deletion cleanup and/or the event processing flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Triplicated permission-evaluation loop in ClientPermissionsV2: hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) all contain identical evaluate/loop/match logic; extract a shared evaluate helper

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, the permission evaluation and scope-matching logic is duplicated across three methods: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` both call `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` and then iterate `for (Permission permission : permissions)` and `for (String s : permission.getScopes())` to check for a matching scope; `hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)` performs the same nested iteration with the same matching intent. This is a diff-grounded maintainability concern (duplication), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission overloads resolve the 'all clients' resource inconsistently: hasPermission(String) uses resourceStore.findByName while hasPermission(ClientModel, String) uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA plus a policy-store existence check, inviting inconsistent behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, the two `hasPermission` overloads do resolve the “all clients” resource differently. `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` first tries `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`, and if missing falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and additionally short-circuits if `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. By contrast, `hasPermission(String)` looks up only `resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId())` and returns `false` if absent, with no analogous fallback/creation and no policy-store short-circuit. This is a concrete inconsistency in resolution logic that could lead to divergent behavior if the resource is not present/created via the same path, even if it may be intentional/benign.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2: unused private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) and unused static import AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE
matched_golden_ids: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that ClientPermissionsV2 defines a private getEvaluationContext method that is never called and should be removed. The candidate explicitly flags the same unused getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) as dead code (and additionally mentions an unused import), so it matches the underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) duplicate the role+permission logic of canManage and should delegate to single-scope helpers

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ClientPermissionsV2.canManageClientScopes()` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` do contain some repeated role/permission checks, but this is not a verifiable defect, and the suggested “single-scope helpers” to delegate to are not present in the shown changes. Also, `canView(ClientScopeModel)` intentionally differs from `canView()` by also accepting `MANAGE` permission (`hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`), so it is not a straight duplicate of `canManage`/`canView` logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Interface javadoc in ClientPermissionEvaluator leaks V1/V2 implementation knowledge ('For V2 only: ...'), which will become stale; version-specific semantics belong in implementing classes' docs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds extensive Javadoc to the `ClientPermissionEvaluator` interface, and multiple method docs explicitly reference version-specific behavior (e.g., “For V2 only: Also if it has permission to ...” in `canManage()`, `canView()`, `canManageClientScopes()`, etc.). This couples the interface contract to the current V1/V2 implementation split and can become stale as versions evolve; such version-scoped semantics would more appropriately live in `ClientPermissionsV2`/other implementing classes’ documentation rather than the interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: registerListener feature check wraps the entire event-handling block, disabling pre-existing role/group/permission cleanup handlers too; the overly broad guard and its coupling to V2's throwing setPermissionsEnabled needs explicit commentary or narrowing

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, the prior unconditional handling of RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent is now entirely wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, meaning those cleanup calls (e.g., `...roles().setPermissionsEnabled(role, false)`, `...clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, `...groups().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`) will no longer run when the feature is disabled. That is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that could leave authz artifacts behind in configurations where permissions exist but the feature flag is off. Additionally, the new `ClientPermissionsV2` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for `setPermissionsEnabled`, so if the listener ends up using the V2 implementation under the same feature flag, the current cleanup call path would become unsafe—this coupling is plausible from the diff, though the exact management() dispatch isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2: AdminPermissions.java listener cleanup calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent, which throws under ClientPermissionsV2, failing client removal or erroring on every delete when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled; same hazard applies to RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent if V2 role/group evaluators share the same throwing stub

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2 where multiple management APIs, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)`, are stubbed to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). In `AdminPermissions.java`, the provider event listener (now gated by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`) still invokes `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent`. If the `management(...).clients()` implementation is the V2 path (supported by `MgmtPermissionsV2` now overriding `clients()` to return `ClientPermissionsV2`), this call will throw during client deletion, causing deletion to error and/or leaving cleanup incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 lost the admin-role fallback, so a realm admin with MANAGE_CLIENTS who passes canManage(client) is denied on mapping client roles, composites, or client-scope roles, breaking normal admin flows

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` are implemented as pure permission checks (`return hasPermission(client, <scope>)`) and do not include any admin-role-based shortcut (e.g., `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`) nor do they defer to `canManage(client)`. Meanwhile `canManage(ClientModel client)` explicitly grants access for `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS`. This creates an inconsistent authorization outcome visible from the diff: a caller with `MANAGE_CLIENTS` can be considered able to manage a client but will still get `false` from these map-* checks unless explicit authz permissions exist, which can deny expected operations guarded by these methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback in ClientPermissionsV2 misses type-based permissions: when the per-client resource doesn't exist, the all-clients fallback gates on findByResource which doesn't return type-associated scope permissions, causing valid global grants to silently deny; this deny path is untested

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel,String), when the per-client Resource is missing it falls back to the type resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)) but then short-circuits with `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` and returns false. This introduces a potentially incorrect deny path if there are relevant scope permissions that are not returned by a resource-bound lookup (e.g., type-based scope permissions), and the diff does not add a targeted test that exercises this fallback+short-circuit behavior. The claim that PolicyStore.findByResource definitively omits type-based permissions is not verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s best treated as an untested/fragile edge case rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 throw UnsupportedOperationException at runtime, yielding a 500 in token-exchange admin checks instead of a clean deny or routed V1 evaluation

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` and `exchangeToPermission(...)` (and related permission builders) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If any V2 execution path calls these methods, it would indeed raise an uncaught runtime exception rather than returning a deny result. However, from this diff alone there is no evidence that token-exchange admin checks actually invoke these methods under V2, or that this results in an HTTP 500 in practice; that part of the finding is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-flag gate on cleanup listeners in AdminPermissions.java skips authz resource cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is disabled, leaving stale orphaned resources/policies if the feature is toggled off after permissions were created

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the listener cleanup logic in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` with `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, on `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` it always called `management(...).*.setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which is the apparent hook to disable/remove fine-grained permissions artifacts when those models are deleted. With the new gate, if the feature is disabled (including after permissions were created), those cleanup calls will not run, plausibly leaving stale authz permission state/resources behind.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 performs N+1 full policy-engine evaluations per client resource with no caching, a likely performance cliff on large realms

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission, the code iterates over every resource of type CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType(...) and for each resource calls hasGrantedPermission(...), which invokes root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...)) (a policy evaluation) per resource. The diff shows no memoization/caching or batched evaluation, so on realms with many client resources this becomes O(N) policy-engine evaluations and can be a performance cliff. This is a performance/architecture concern rather than a directly verifiable correctness defect.
